labels.name: Myoglobin
labels.function: Binds and stores O2, shuttling it toward mitochondria

labels.name: Phosphocreatine
labels.function: High-energy phosphate donor; depleted in about 10 seconds

labels.name: Creatine kinase
labels.function: Single-step anaerobic ATP regeneration; serum injury marker

labels.name: Glycogen
labels.function: Stored fuel mobilized by Ca-calmodulin and epinephrine

labels.name: GLUT4
labels.function: Imports blood sugar across the sarcolemma

labels.name: Pyruvate
labels.function: End product of glycolysis; its fate depends on O2

labels.name: Lactate
labels.function: Made when O2 is limited; accompanies, not causes, fatigue

labels.name: Pyruvate dehydrogenase
labels.function: Converts the glycolytic end product for mitochondrial entry

labels.name: Acetyl CoA
labels.function: Two-carbon unit that feeds the mitochondrial cycle

labels.name: TCA cycle
labels.function: Generates NADH and FADH2 from two-carbon units

labels.name: Electron transport chain
labels.function: O2-dependent ATP production: ~32 ATP per glucose

labels.name: Small motor neuron
labels.function: Lowest threshold; drives a unit of ~100-500 fibers

labels.name: Large motor neuron
labels.function: Highest threshold; drives a unit of ~1000-2000 fibers

labels.name: Type I fiber
labels.function: Slow, fatigue-resistant; dominates soleus and paraspinals

labels.name: Type IIA fiber
labels.function: Fast but oxidative-glycolytic; supports sustained power

labels.name: Type IIX fiber
labels.function: Fast, high-force, rapidly fatigable sprint fiber

labels.name: Capillary
labels.function: Delivers O2 by diffusion; densest around slow fibers

labels.name: Mitochondrion
labels.function: Site of oxidative phosphorylation (~30-32 ATP/glucose)

labels.name: Lipid droplet
labels.function: Ready fat fuel store, high in oxidative fibers

labels.name: Glycogen granules
labels.function: Supplies rapid anaerobic ATP; depletes quickly
